catalog_quote: El mazateco de Ixcatlán es una lengua de acento fijo, por lo que es predecible ya que ocurre siempre en la última sílaba de las raíces, y cumple con la función demarcativa de indicar en donde finalizan las palabras. Por lo tanto, en esta lengua no existen pares mínimos acentuales como en español, donde algunas palabras se distinguen por la posición donde recae el acento, e.g., “papa” vs. “papá”. Kager (2007) menciona que normalmente es más común que las lenguas eviten la posición final para asignar el acento, prefiriendo sílabas iniciales o antepenúltimas, por lo que el MZI representa un contraejemplo a esta tendencia tipológica. [...] En este punto podemos generalizar que el patrón acentual del MZI es de prominencia final obligatoria; es un tipo de acento demarcativo, esto es, no es contrastivo léxicamente pero es necesario para marcar el final de las raíces, por lo que todas las palabras emergen con un patrón yámbico obligatorio. [...] Las sílabas tónicas son aquellas donde recae el acento de la palabra. Como se ha indicado anteriormente, el acento en esta lengua siempre ocurre en el margen derecho de la palabra sin importar la longitud de esta

new_statements.quote: Una vez definidos los correlatos fonéticos del acento en MZI, es necesario hablar de su estatus fonológico. El mazateco de Ixcatlán es una lengua de acento fijo, por lo que es predecible ya que ocurre siempre en la última sílaba de las raíces, y cumple con la función demarcativa de indicar en donde finalizan las palabras. Por lo tanto, en esta lengua no existen pares mínimos acentuales como en español [...] (p.233) [...] En este punto podemos generalizar que el patrón acentual del MZI es de prominencia final obligatoria; es un tipo de acento demarcativo, esto es, no es contrastivo léxicamente pero es necesario para marcar el final de las raíces, por lo que todas las palabras emergen con un patrón yámbico obligatorio. (p.235)
new_statements.translation: Having defined the phonetic correlates of stress in Ixcatlán Mazatec (MZI), we must discuss its phonological status. Ixcatlán Mazatec is a fixed-stress language; stress is predictable since it always occurs on the last syllable of roots, and it fulfils the demarcative function of indicating where words end. Hence there are no stress minimal pairs in this language as there are in Spanish [...] At this point we can generalize that the stress pattern of MZI is obligatory final prominence; it is a demarcative type of stress, i.e. not lexically contrastive but needed to mark the end of roots, so all words surface with an obligatory iambic pattern.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File checked: (331 pp., text; extracted text). Quote: both halves are present verbatim. p.247 (printed 233), sec. 5.3.3 'Fonologizacion': "Una vez definidos los correlatos foneticos del acento en MZI, es necesario hablar de su estatus fonologico. El mazateco de Ixcatlan es una lengua de acento fijo, por lo que es predecible ya que ocurre siempre en la ultima silaba de las raices, y cumple con la funcion demarcativa de indicar en donde finalizan las palabras. Por lo tanto, en esta lengua no existen pares minimos acentuales como en espanol, donde.." (continues with papa/papá and a Kager 2007 remark that MZI is a typological counterexample to final-stress avoidance). p.249 (printed 235), after…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls invariably on the final syllable of the (root-final) word; it is non-contrastive and demarcative. Spanish loans are re-stressed on their final syllable (bisiˈkleta -> final stress). Only proclitics exist (p.267), so nothing follows the stressed root syllable within the word. Phonetic correlates are vowel duration and full vowel quality (unstressed vowels reduce/neutralize), not intensity or F0 (tones are independent).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Tentative (pp.266-267): in trisyllabic words some speakers build an extra iambic foot whose sole syllable gets secondary stress on the word-initial syllable, (ˌσ)(σ.ˈσ), evidenced by non-reduction of prefix /tʃo1-/; other speakers leave that syllable unfooted σ(σ.ˈσ). Author says more evidence is needed; only one primary stress per word.
new_statements.exceptions: None for primary stress; author notes Kirk 1966 reports some trochaic items in Chiquihuitlán (a different variety). Some roots with semantically transparent added morphemes keep full vowel quality in unstressed position (p.233), an allophony exception, not a stress-placement exception.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain stated as the root / word right edge ('última sílaba de las raíces', 'margen derecho de la palabra sin importar la longitud', p.259); native words are 1-3 syllables; recent Spanish loans keep all syllables with final stress; clitics are proclitic only. Data: Kirk wordlist elicitation, speakers from Nuevo Ixcatlán and Chichicazapa (resettled San Pedro Ixcatlán communities), acoustic measurements from one older male speaker.
new_statements.identity_note: Source describes 'mazateco de Ixcatlán (MZI)', 'én ni̱ngo̱ tsie, the Mazatec of San Pedro Ixcatlán municipality (Oaxaca) and its resettled communities Nuevo Ixcatlán (Playa Vicente, Veracruz) and Chichicazapa (San Miguel Soyaltepec) after the Miguel Alemán dam; = Glottolog ixca1246 / ISO mzi. The author distinguishes it from 'tenanguero' ('én ngat'iá), a second Mazatec lect also spoken in San Pedro Ixcatlán municipality, which is not the object of description. Not to be confused with Ixcatec (ixca1245, Popolocan).

new_statements.quote: Words in San Pedro de Ixcatlán Mazatec (Ix) contain a stressed syllable which may be preceeded by up to three pre-stressed syllables. Words never exhibit more than one post-stressed syllable. Stress is predictable in that it always occurs on the ultimate syllable of the stem. It is not contrastive and need not be written. The post-stressed syllables are enclitics. Rhythm segments my [sic] contain from one to four syllables with stress on the ultimate syllable. In this paper hyphens are used to separate enclitics from the final syllable of the stem.

new_statements.relation_note: Same placement as the catalog rule (fixed final) and as Wagner Oviedo 2018 sec. 5.3.3 (final syllable of the root, demarcative, predictable). Wagner Oviedo 2018:226 already cites Lamiman for final stress; Lamiman adds the non-contrastive status, the stem-final (not word-final) domain with enclitics after the stress, and the stressed/unstressed syllable-shape asymmetries.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the last syllable of the stem (root), always and predictably; it is non-contrastive and not. Up to three unstressed syllables may precede it; anything after it is an enclitic (at most one post-stressed syllable in a word, though an example with two enclitic syllables is also given). Four contrastive tones operate independently of stress (sec. 4). Stressed syllables admit any consonant cluster, nasal vowels and vowel clusters; unstressed syllables are restricted (no glottal stop in CV, no nasal vowels, a~o free variation, no vowel clusters except in loans) (secs. 2.1-2.4, pp.4-6).
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; enclitics follow the stressed stem-final syllable ('post-stressed syllables are enclitics'), so the stressed syllable is final in the stem, not necessarily in the phonological word. Data from one speaker, Mario Ignacio de Jesús of Chichicazapa (Soyaltepec district), presented as San Pedro Ixcatlán Mazatec.
new_statements.identity_note: Lamiman's data come from a single speaker of Chichicazapa (Soyaltepec district, Oaxaca), which he labels San Pedro de Ixcatlán Mazatec (Ix) = mzi; Wagner Oviedo 2018 describes 'én ni̱ngo̱ tsie of San Pedro Ixcatlán / Soyaltepec / Playa Vicente, the same lowland variety. Both are Ixcatlán Mazatec [mzi], not the Popolocan Ixcatec.

tone_statements.quote: el MZI se define como una lengua tonal debido a que la tonía ... permite distinguir significados léxicos o gramaticales (Crystal, 2008; Yip, 2002). En esta lengua existen tres tonos primarios, los cuales se distinguen por la altura a la que se emiten: alto (+agudo), medio y bajo (+grave). ... se sigue asumiendo la propuesta de Wagner (2018) respecto a la existencia de tres tonos de nivel primarios en el MZI, los cuales forman los primitivos distintivos de esta lengua. ... esto implica que, como ya se mencionó más arriba, los tonos de contorno se analizan como secuencias de tonos de nivel.
tone_statements.translation: MZI is defined as a tonal language because pitch ... allows lexical or grammatical meanings to be distinguished. In this language there are three primary tones, distinguished by the height at which they are produced: high, mid and low. ... we continue to assume Wagner's (2018) proposal of three primary level tones in MZI, which form the distinctive primitives of this language. ... this implies that, as already mentioned, contour tones are analysed as sequences of level tones.
tone_statements.locator: p.16, introduction; and p.25, sec. 'Propuesta analítica'
tone_statements.summary: Three level tones H/M/L plus underlyingly toneless roots (default L); contours = level sequences; floating tones; declination and automatic downstep (downdrift) via Praat; stress final on base.

tone_statements.citation: Wagner Oviedo, Carlos de Jesús. 2018. Xi kó ts'en fañe 'én ni̱ngo̱tsie: Fonología segmental y tonal del mazateco de Ixcatlán. Tesis de licenciatura en Lingüística, Escuela Nacional de Antropología e Historia / INAH, México.
tone_statements.quote: El MZI es una lengua tonal, esto es, cuenta con distinciones léxicas a partir del uso contrastivo de la velocidad controlada del movimiento longitudinal de las cuerdas vocales ... En términos fonológicos, el MZI cuenta con cuatro categorías fonológicas tonales representadas con superíndices numéricos donde se correlaciona la agudeza del tono en cuestión con un número más alto en la representación subyacente: tono alto (a 3), tono medio (a2), tono bajo (a1) y no tono (a). El no tono hace referencia a que la palabra o sílaba en cuestión no cuenta con una especificación tonal en la subyacencia.
tone_statements.translation: MZI is a tonal language, that is, it has lexical distinctions based on the contrastive use of the controlled speed of the longitudinal movement of the vocal folds ... In phonological terms, MZI has four tonal phonological categories represented with numerical superscripts, where a higher pitch correlates with a higher number in the underlying representation: high tone (a3), mid tone (a2), low tone (a1) and no tone (a). 'No tone' means that the word or syllable in question has no tonal specification underlyingly.
tone_statements.summary: Three level tones H/M/L plus an underlying toneless category (surfaces low by default); floating tones (2sg possessive = floating L) give contours on long vowels; stress fixed on base-final syllable.

sources.note: Sec. 5.3 'Acento' pp.225-235: fixed, predictable stress always on the last syllable of the root/word (demarcative, iambic, right-prominent); no stress minimal pairs; Spanish loans re-stressed on the final syllable (OT tableaux pp.234-235); phonetic correlates measured (60 tokens, Praat): duration and vowel quality, not intensity or F0 (p.233); p.226 endorses Lamiman's final-stress proposal; pp.266-267 tentative secondary stress on the first syllable of trisyllables for some speakers; p.259 stress at right edge regardless of word length; p.276 conclusions restate iambic final stress.
